final_recommendation: The room converged on a disciplined underwriting framework requiring vendor-control attestations, auditor-rotation disclosure, and single-aggregate reinsurance limits for correlated audit failures—but exposed a critical unresolved gap: whether the three banks' D&O counsel have coordinated messaging protocols to prevent simultaneous public disclosures that could trigger depositor runs. The room terminated with forensic attestation review underway but the contagion-control mechanism (joint messaging) unenforceable.
minority_objections: Emerging risk lead and AI agent analyst repeatedly flagged that coordinated messaging protocols cannot be enforced if banks are competitors in the same markets—boards will fragment disclosures to distance themselves regardless of counsel agreements
Claims counsel raised that if attestations show burial (not disclosure) of KPMG deficiencies, the tail shifts from litigation duration to systemic contagion—a fundamentally different reserving model
key_conflicts: Financial lines underwriter pushed for policy-condition enforcement of joint messaging protocols; emerging risk lead countered that competitive incentives make such protocols unenforceable when banks operate in the same deposit markets

Reinsurance manager wanted single-aggregate limits locked immediately; claims counsel insisted on waiting for attestation forensics to determine warranty recovery leverage before finalizing treaty language
D&O specialist demanded locked messaging protocols before renewal; AI agent analyst questioned whether making it a policy condition versus an observed-risk flag actually changes bank behavior
key_concessions: Financial lines underwriter conceded that vendor attestations must be cross-checked against live claims discovery files (KPMG/PwC) in real time, not just accepted at face value
Reinsurance manager accepted that single-aggregate language must explicitly define 'correlated' (shared auditor, same audit period, overlapping control deficiency) to prevent reinsurer disputes
Claims counsel agreed to accelerate attestation forensics to end of R5 (two weeks) to unblock reinsurance treaty exclusion language
D&O specialist conceded to pull counsel contact lists and force messaging protocol conversation into underwriting record, even without direct knowledge of current coordination status
red_lines: Financial lines underwriter: non-renewal if banks cannot produce vendor-stack attestation within 60 days—holding unaudited exposure is worse than losing premium
Claims counsel: if attestations show material misrepresentation (buried KPMG deficiencies), warranty breach triggers separate recovery action and tightens underwriting gate
Reinsurance manager: will not renew treaties without explicit single-aggregate-limit clauses for correlated audit failures—independent-claim interpretation by reinsurers is unacceptable
D&O specialist: if three banks' counsel won't lock joint messaging protocol, that becomes a written red flag attached to every reinsurance renewal
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: The room never resolved whether the three banks are actually competitors in the same deposit markets—if they are, the joint messaging protocol is structurally unenforceable regardless of policy conditions
No one quantified the speed of depositor flight if three simultaneous 'auditor failed' disclosures hit social media—the room assumed hours-to-collapse but provided no empirical basis
The room did not address what happens if KPMG settles before the attestation forensics complete—the coordination window for subrogation recovery could close before the underwriting gate fires
AI agent analyst raised automation of correlation triggers to scale discipline under stress, but the room never operationalized what that automation would look like or who owns it
downstream_risk_variables: Attestation forensics outcome: disclosed vs. buried audit deficiencies (determines warranty recovery leverage)
D&O counsel coordination status: locked joint messaging protocol vs. fragmented disclosures
Geographic/competitive overlap of three banks (determines enforceability of messaging protocols)
KPMG settlement timing vs. attestation forensics completion (coordination window for subrogation)
Reinsurance treaty language specificity: definition of 'correlated' claims
Defense-cost overlap period (Q1-Q3 2026 when KPMG and PwC both live)
Clash sublimit adequacy for simultaneous defense costs across multiple insureds
uncertainty_notes: The room achieved underwriting discipline on attestation requirements and reinsurance treaty structure, but left three critical uncertainties unresolved: (1) whether the three banks are competitors in the same markets, which determines if joint messaging protocols are enforceable; (2) the actual speed and mechanism of depositor flight if disclosures fragment—the room assumed hours-to-collapse but provided no data; (3) whether KPMG settles before attestation forensics complete, closing the subrogation coordination window. The room also never operationalized the AI agent analyst's automation proposal for correlation triggers under stress.
